execution_contract.executor: a fallible model -- after the 2026-11-01 restart that is DeepSeek, and the shape is written so a different model does not invalidate it
execution_contract.written_because: a task written for a careful reader fails differently under a model that would rather produce a paragraph than a command: 'implement X' has no predicate, so every output satisfies it and the cheapest satisfying output is a summary claiming success. The shape moves the refusal into the task, so the executor cannot satisfy it by describing it.

known_failure_modes.mode: declares success in prose ("this passes", "done", "looks right") without running anything
known_failure_modes.check_that_fires: T2 predicate-runnable + T5 no-acceptance in tools/task_shape_check.py

known_failure_modes.mode: satisfies the letter: implements the happy path, never exercises the refusal, so a broken gate reads as working
known_failure_modes.check_that_fires: T3 control-present (a control that is not something REFUSED is itself refused)

known_failure_modes.mode: deletes the obstacle -- a test, a claim, a gate, a detector -- to make the run green
re-scopes the task to something easier and reports the easier thing as the task
known_failure_modes.check_that_fires: T1 shape-complete (deliverable) + the frame's rule 4 (do not narrow, widen or improve the intent)

known_failure_modes.mode: answers a question instead of doing the work, at length
known_failure_modes.check_that_fires: T2 predicate-runnable; a task whose acceptance cannot be run is not shipped as a task

known_failure_modes.mode: reports a detector that could not run as zero findings
known_failure_modes.check_that_fires: T4 evidence-lands (a path or command, never a promise) + FLAMING SWORD's UNRUN rule

known_failure_modes.mode: claims a control is in place without exercising it (RULE 0B-D)
known_failure_modes.check_that_fires: the tool's own --selftest, which must be the evidence named

known_failure_modes.mode: over-generalises one incident into a universal rule that decides nothing
known_failure_modes.check_that_fires: META-LEVELS-CANON Heaven tests: name the decision class and three trajectories, or drop the rule

how_the_shape_defends: the finish line is a command and an outcome, so "describe the result" and "produce the result" stop looking alike
the control is a mutation that MUST be refused, so a happy path cannot masquerade as a test
the refusal is written before the work, so the executor cannot choose the landing condition after seeing what it built
the evidence field names where the proof lands, so a claim with nowhere to land is visible as empty
legacy tasks are counted and printed, not failed: a gate that retroactively fails finished work teaches routing-around, not rigor
ritual: 1. read the task's four fields before writing code; if any is missing, the task is not ready and that is a finding, not an obstacle
2. run the control FIRST: introduce the defect, watch the predicate fail
3. do the work; never delete a test, claim or gate -- if one must go, name what it defended in the commit
4. run the acceptance command and quote its output in the commit body (the `Verified:` line)
5. if the acceptance cannot be run, STOP and report which field failed; a frame report is a finished turn, a summary is not

E.name: Sword dissection and render shards
E.one_line: a FLAMING SWORD that dissects game code into captured units, mints them as Shards under the M-01 contract, and composes them into a player's own game -- including 3D render shards -- without ever shipping a unit whose rights the extractor cannot show

G.name: Revival -- discontinued games converted into shards
G.one_line: ship the rules, hash the assets: a shard converts a discontinued game's simulation and configuration by MEASUREMENT, refuses to contain a byte of the original, and will not start without the player's own copy -- because the EU declined to legislate (2026) and the US declined a preservation exemption (2024)

H.name: Resurrection -- the Atari 2600 as the first repairable machine (right-to-repair framing)
H.gates: M-31 -> M-32 -> M-33 -> M-34 -> M-35 -> M-36 -> M-37, with M-38 (orchestrator) usable now and M-39 (cartridge source) decided
H.one_line: the owner already owns the cartridge and the machine is what died, so the repair is the emulator -- which Sony v. Connectix (2000) already held is fair use: implement the hardware, keep the cartridge, never decrypt and never patch, and let the shard carry the rules plus a hash lock to the owner's own image
H.why_the_2600_first: 1.19 MHz 6507, fixed 76x262 frame, 128 bytes of RAM, 160x192 beam-raced display, integer only -- every 2600 game is ALREADY a deterministic frame-locked simulation, so conversion is separating two things the hardware forced together, not translating into a foreign model

X.name: Defensive execution -- tasks written to survive a fallible model
X.one_line: a task is a predicate plus a refusal, not a sentence: the gate in the task file (M-40) and the defender prompter in FLAMING SWORD (M-41) exist so the executor cannot satisfy a task by describing it, and the sweep loop refuses a batch with no frame (M-42)

right_to_repair_goals.title: An owner can resurrect a cartridge they already own on modern hardware, without acquiring anything they do not own
right_to_repair_goals.measure: one 2600 cartridge converted and played on Windows/Ubuntu/Kali from the owner's own image, with zero bytes of that image in the shard

right_to_repair_goals.title: The conversion proves itself by measurement, not by a reviewer's opinion
right_to_repair_goals.measure: a divergence counter over >= 10,000 ticks per scenario family, with a first-divergence tick named on every failure

right_to_repair_goals.title: Resurrected games run on the bleeding edge without changing how they play
right_to_repair_goals.measure: one state hash across >= 3 presentation tiers (tier 0 = the original hardware class), 120/240 Hz presentation over a native-rate sim, verifiable score runs

right_to_repair_goals.title: The 2600 becomes the argument that unlocks the harder cases (16-bit, DOS, dead MMOs)
right_to_repair_goals.measure: a written legal + engineering record from this track that Track G cites for its own classes instead of re-deriving them

hardware.reference: one Windows laptop with integrated graphics, the Ubuntu-26.04 WSL host and the Kali host; a 4 GB-RAM machine for M-11
hardware.budget_source: M-02 replaces every provisional number with a reading or a recorded waiver

tasks.title: Shard manifest spec v1 (shard.json + JSON Schema)
tasks.deliverable: docs/METTHEW/shard.schema.json + prose in the plan: id, version, genre, files, entrypoint, loader, golden_run {input, ticks, state_sha256, token}, hubs[], budget, licence, author_pubkey, execution_model, env_allowlist, tick_budget, competitive, provenance
tasks.acceptance: validates the three M-05 shards; rejects 5 named malformed fixtures (missing golden run, undeclared hub, oversize payload, entry outside shard, duplicate id) with the offending field named
tasks.risk: a schema that only fits one genre will be rewritten by M-05; keep the engine out of the schema

tasks.title: Low-end budget bench
tasks.deliverable: tools/metthew_bench.py + budget.json (load, tick cost, peak RSS, validator wall clock, play fps at 720p)
tasks.acceptance: three runs per scene, numbers reproducible within 10%; every provisional plan number replaced by a reading or a recorded waiver; the failing numbers are published, not rounded
tasks.risk: measuring on a fast host and calling it 'low-end' would invalidate every later gate; the box is named in the record

tasks.title: Validator tools/metthew_validate.py
tasks.deliverable: static liftability check (no reference escapes the shard), hub declaration check, payload budget, golden run, determinism re-run, JSON report, exit codes, --selftest
tasks.acceptance: pass/block on 3 fixtures in the tests; a shard with one external reference is blocked and the blocker is named with graph + ref count; a shard that fakes its state hash is blocked; exit 0 only when every gate passes
tasks.risk: an oracle that has never failed is not an oracle -- the negative controls ship in the same change (RULE 0B-C)

tasks.title: Minting CLI: metthew mint <name>
tasks.deliverable: scaffold manifest, golden run, self-test, placeholder scene; run the validator; print the exact next command
tasks.acceptance: mint -> validate -> play in <=10 minutes on the reference box with no toolchain beyond python3; the scaffolded shard is green before it is edited
tasks.risk: a scaffolder that hides the manifest teaches nothing; the manifest must be the first file a gamer reads

tasks.title: Three reference shards, three genres
tasks.deliverable: 2-player arena; single-player puzzle; doc+data-only rule set/roster pack; each <=24 files
tasks.acceptance: all three validate green on Windows/Ubuntu/Kali; arena and puzzle run at 720p/30 on the reference box; the doc-only shard loads with zero code
tasks.risk: three from one author still share that author's blind spots; M-10's play test is the counterweight

tasks.title: Deterministic play ledger and replay verifier
tasks.deliverable: fixed-step sim, input log, per-tick state hash chain, replay verifier, documented numeric policy
tasks.acceptance: same input log -> identical hash on all three hosts; a flipped input byte diverges at a named tick; 20-minute session replays in <=2 s
tasks.risk: float and iteration-order drift will look like cheating; a numeric policy (fixed-point or bounded float) is part of the task, not a follow-up

tasks.title: Exploit-as-content: antibody shard for game exploits
tasks.deliverable: signature/probe/instances/status shard in the shape of src/SHARDS/antibodies.py, with seeking -> neutralized -> immune tied to recorded seek evidence
tasks.acceptance: one real exploit demo cloned into a probe that finds it in 3 fixture shards and in none of 3 clean shards (positive and negative control); status cannot advance without the recorded seek
tasks.risk: an antibody that fires on healthy shards splits a circle faster than cheating does

tasks.title: Bundle exchange (USB / LAN / chat)
tasks.deliverable: one-file bundle (payload + manifest + hash), metthew add <bundle>, verify-then-play; the circle's shard list is a local file
tasks.acceptance: a tampered bundle is refused with the hash mismatch named; a bundle over budget is refused by the budget gate; installing requires no network
tasks.risk: file exchange does not scale past a circle; M-10 records that boundary rather than papering over it

tasks.title: Local reputation: signed result files
tasks.deliverable: signed result file (shard id, version, state hash, score, witnesses) that travels with the bundle
tasks.acceptance: forged score fails signature; a result whose shard version/hash does not match the installed shard is rejected; no global ranking is implied or stored
tasks.risk: signature files are not a reputation system; the plan says what they cannot do (Sybil, collusion) in the player-facing text

tasks.title: Circle protocol + 3-person play test
tasks.deliverable: written procedure: how a circle starts, mints, shares, contests, retires; plus the write-up of a real 3-person run with timings
tasks.acceptance: mint -> share -> play -> contest -> retire completed with no central service; every step names the command that performed it and how long it took
tasks.risk: a play test with the author present tests the author; one participant must be the non-author who runs the commands

tasks.title: Portability matrix
tasks.deliverable: matrix of validator + one reference shard across Windows 10/11 iGPU, Ubuntu-26.04, Kali, and one 4 GB-RAM host
tasks.acceptance: one row per host, pass/fail per gate, and the exact failing command for every fail; no host is reported green without a run
tasks.risk: green on the author's machine is the default outcome; the matrix exists to make that inadmissible

tasks.title: Project gates: unplayable ratchet + weekly cold run
tasks.deliverable: baseline of unplayable shards that may fall and never rise (the unresolved-ratchet pattern) plus a scheduled cold run
tasks.acceptance: ratchet fails on a newly unplayable shard and passes on a fix; --selftest runs with its negative control; a stale baseline is reported stale rather than trusted
tasks.risk: a ratchet nobody runs is a comment; the scheduled run is part of the acceptance, not a later convenience

tasks.title: Dissection contract: what a captured unit IS
tasks.deliverable: docs/METTHEW/dissection.spec.json + tools/sword_dissect.py --check: a unit is {kind: feature|function|effect|controller|config, capability_id, provenance{source_repo, source_path, source_commit, licence, licence_evidence}, bounds{files, bytes}, interface{inputs, outputs, tick_affects}, evidence{entrypoints, tests}}
tasks.acceptance: refuses a unit with no licence, no source_commit, an unknown capability_id (not in highend_families.json), or tick_affects=sim with determinism!=exact; a seeded fixture of 3 valid + 4 invalid units gives 3 PASS and 4 named REFUSALs
tasks.risk: a contract that describes only Python cannot capture a controller written in another language; keep kind and interface language-neutral or the first real extraction rewrites the schema

tasks.title: Sword dissection engine (static capture of units)
tasks.deliverable: tools/sword_dissect.py --repo <path> --emit units.jsonl: AST pass that finds candidate features/functions/effects/controllers/configs, classifies each by what it touches (state, input, render, config), and refuses anything whose closure it cannot bound
tasks.acceptance: on a seeded tree with 3 extractable units and 2 decoys -- one with a hidden import, one whose effect reaches the simulation through a global -- emits exactly 3 and names both decoys with the reason; an empty tree emits 0 units and says so instead of guessing
tasks.risk: static capture is the easiest place to over-claim: a unit that is only 'mostly' captured must be refused, because a half-captured effect is a bug the player cannot see

tasks.title: Provenance and licence gate for captured code
tasks.deliverable: the gate between extraction and minting: each unit carries licence + licence_evidence + source_commit; a mint records the chain into shard.provenance, and a composition may not mix incompatible licences
tasks.acceptance: 4 fixtures: MIT accepted, unknown licence refused, a GPL unit into an MIT shard refused, mixed set refused with both licences named; a unit whose source_commit is absent cannot be minted at all
tasks.risk: dissecting game code is only lawful where the extractor can show the rights -- this gate is the difference between a tool and a liability, so it lands BEFORE minting and never after

tasks.title: Mint a Shard from captured units
tasks.deliverable: sword_dissect.py --mint <units> --out <dir>: writes a Metthew shard (manifest + files + golden_run) whose capability ids come from highend_families.json and whose id is content-addressed over the captured set
tasks.acceptance: the minted shard passes tools/metthew_validate.py including V7/V9 and the families vocabulary check; a unit set that cannot produce a deterministic golden run is refused with the failing unit named
tasks.risk: minting turns a research artefact into something a friend will run; the golden run must be generated by execution, never copied from the source game

tasks.title: Compose captured units into the player's own game
tasks.deliverable: sword_dissect.py --compose <unit>... --out <dir>: resolves the unit interfaces, refuses conflicts (two units claiming the same tick channel, two controllers owning the same config key) instead of last-write-wins, and emits one shard with a single golden run
tasks.acceptance: 3 units captured from 2 different source trees compose into a shard that runs and whose hash is stable across two processes; two units with conflicting tick_affects are refused and both ids are named
tasks.risk: composition is where extraction stops being a demo: without refusal semantics the sword silently produces a game whose rules nobody wrote

tasks.title: 3D render shards out of the sword
tasks.deliverable: the sword emits render shards in the catalogue's presentation families (glassland, spectra, fogcut, splatfield, ladder), always dual-layer: an exact integer sim plus a declared presentation tier ladder and a headless golden run
tasks.acceptance: an emitted render shard is ladder-class and its --verify proves ONE state hash across at least 3 tiers while the presentation counters differ; a shard whose renderer is allowed to touch the sim is refused by V7
tasks.risk: the only render shards testable on this box are the sim half and the ladder; the splat/path/neural halves need a native host and must be declared unverified until one exists

tasks.title: Revival classes R0-R4 in the manifest, with the refusals they imply

evidence.claim: 1,294,188 verified statements submitted; Commission declined to propose new legislation
US Copyright Office declined a new preservation exemption; renewed exemptions run Oct 2027-Oct 2030
87% of classic US releases are out of print and critically endangered
NCSoft granted Homecoming a limited licence to run and develop City of Heroes
clean-room reimplementations ship no game code and require the player's own data

tasks.deliverable: a `revival` block in shard.schema.json: class R0|R1|R2|R3|R4, source_game, clean_room, ships_original_bytes, requires_assets, behaviour_evidence; plus validator rules V14 (R2 may not declare shareable), V15 (class R4 is not a shard at all), V16 (R1 with ships_original_bytes true is refused)
tasks.acceptance: 5 class fixtures: R0-R3 validate, R4 refused with the reason recorded; an R2 bundle marked shareable is refused naming V14; an R1 shard whose file list contains the source game's own bytes is refused naming V16
tasks.risk: classes invite false precision -- a rights question settled by a JSON field is not settled at all; the class records what the author asserts, and the evidence field must be printable so a reader can disagree with the assertion

tasks.title: Asset lock and null-assets CI mode
tasks.deliverable: requires_assets.files[{path, sha256, size_bytes}] checked at load, with a refusal naming the file and both hashes; and a --null-assets mode that runs the golden run against synthetic stand-ins so CI never needs the original game
tasks.acceptance: a missing file refuses; a mismatched hash refuses and prints expected vs found; --null-assets runs the golden run headless and reproduces the declared state hash exactly, while declaring in its output that the asset half is unproven
tasks.risk: too strict a lock refuses a legitimate owner with a different regional release; too loose a lock quietly runs on the wrong data. Declare the granularity and make the refusal message specific enough to diagnose without the author

tasks.title: Behaviour capture protocol: measure, do not decompile
tasks.deliverable: a scenario schema (fixed inputs, fixed tick count) plus a divergence counter that compares an observed transition trace with a reimplementation's, reporting first-divergence tick and the offending field
tasks.acceptance: recording the same scenario twice yields 0 divergences; injecting a one-tick input offset yields >0 divergences with the first divergent tick named; the counter is exercised on a scenario of >= 10000 ticks
tasks.risk: divergence of 0 on one scenario is not fidelity; the protocol needs a matrix (movement, combat, economy, timing) or it will certify a game whose jump feels wrong

tasks.title: Config and data extraction into a config shard, class-gated
tasks.deliverable: parse a discontinued game's tables into typed, ranged, integerised config units with a provenance record per table; R2 by default when the source is a proprietary binary, and the sword refuses to bundle an R2 unit for sharing
tasks.acceptance: the extracted table reproduces the recorded outcomes on at least 20 worked cases; a table derived from a proprietary file is stamped R2 and the bundle command refuses with the reason; a public-domain table is stamped R0 and bundles
tasks.risk: a derived table is a derived copy; the sword must never launder it into 'new data' by renaming fields, and the refusal has to be structural rather than advisory

tasks.title: sword revive: identify -> class -> assets -> behaviour -> sim -> mint
tasks.deliverable: one CLI that takes a discontinued game's install directory and emits either an R1 asset-free shard (shareable) or a refusal naming the stage that failed and the class it would have required
tasks.acceptance: a synthetic 'dead game' fixture converts to an R1 shard that runs under --null-assets and passes metthew_validate.py; the same fixture with a fake DRM marker is refused at the class stage as R4 with no bundle written
tasks.risk: the sword must never gain a decryption path. A 'convenience' switch added under pressure is the single change that turns this project into the thing the 2024 rulemaking refused to protect

tasks.title: Revival ladder and compose: the old game's feel as a capability
tasks.deliverable: every revival shard declares >= 3 presentation tiers (the original's hardware class as tier 0), and a composed shard may graft a revived controller onto new rules without copying the original's presentation
tasks.acceptance: the revival shard proves one state hash across its tiers (reusing the ladder gate); composing a revived controller with a new rules shard yields a shard whose hash is stable across two processes while its tier-0 presentation drops everything the original could not draw
tasks.risk: compose is where a revival quietly becomes a rerelease; the composition must carry the source shard's class and refuse to upgrade R1 into R0 by assembly

tasks.title: Cartridge intake: identify, hash, decode, classify, with no output path for a modified image
tasks.deliverable: tools/sword_2600.py --inspect <rom> (DELIVERED 2026-11-01): size/mapper intake for 2K-64K, sha256 identity as the asset lock, documented-6502 recursive decode from the RESET vector with branches/JMP/JSR, TIA/RIOT/RAM/ROM classification of every operand, hardware profile (WSYNC/VSYNC, graphics registers, RIOT timers, collision reads, controller reads) and per-game CLASS advice phrased as what the conversion must do
tasks.acceptance: 27 decode controls + 4 scan controls pass under --selftest; tests/test_sword_2600.py 7 checks green under the 3.15t interpreter; the report declares shipped_original_bytes false; an unknown cartridge size is refused rather than guessed; a RESET vector outside the image is refused; a stream of undocumented opcodes decodes to 0 instructions instead of a plausible guess

evidence.selftest: SELFTEST OK (27 decode controls, 4 scan controls)

limits: documented opcodes only -- some 2600 games use undocumented instructions for size
one bank: a static scan sees the bank mapped at load, not the others
no TIA model, so no cycle-exact capture yet (that is M-33)
makes no claim about the game's rules (that is M-34)
tasks.risk: intake is the only stage where a wrong answer looks like a good report: an unknown mapper guessed as 4K produces confident nonsense. Refuse instead of guessing

tasks.title: Bank-switching model: F8 / F6 / F4 / E0 / 3F
tasks.deliverable: a mapper layer (DELIVERED 2026-11-01): MapperSpec + modelled schemes F8/F6/F4/FE/3F, a (bank, offset) worklist so the scan follows a switch into the new bank at the instruction after the switching access, per-bank code/data split, the switch list with resume addresses, and scheme selection by MEASUREMENT rather than by size
tasks.acceptance: DONE 2026-11-01 -- an 8K F8 fixture reaches both banks and proves the far side is visible only past the switch; FE is measured over F8 on the same geometry; a wrong hot-spot (forced F8) reports bank 0 NOT REACHED while still reporting the entry bank's 4 instructions, so it is not a zero-code image; two schemes touched -> 'ambiguous'; a 64K image (no modelled scheme) is refused; 3F resolves the bank from the value written to $003F

evidence.selftest: SELFTEST OK (27 decode controls, 11 scan controls, 15 mapper controls)
evidence.measured_f8: mapper F8 x2 of 4096 bytes, entry bank 1, 2 of 2 banks reached, bank 1 -> bank 0 at 0xf004 via 0x1ff8, resume 0xf007, 6 instructions / 14 bytes code across both banks
evidence.measured_wrong_hotspot: forced F8 on a switch at $1ff0: 1 of 2 banks reached, bank 0 0 instr NOT REACHED, bank 1 entry 4 instr; verdict names the unreached bank rather than calling it empty

limits: E0, E7, F6SC, F4SC, 3E and DPC are named as unmodelled and refused rather than approximated
3F resolves the bank only when the immediate written to $003F is visible in the same linear run; otherwise the switch is reported UNRESOLVED, never assumed to be bank 0
a 64K image is refused outright: no modelled scheme covers it, and reporting it as one window would decode switch accesses as ordinary stores
RORG placement (code assembled for $F000 but switched at $F800) is not modelled; 3F shards must declare their RORG in the report and the note says so
tasks.risk: a wrong hot-spot produces a plausible-looking wrong game. The negative control (wrong address -> explicit failure) is the whole acceptance, not a nicety

tasks.title: Raster-kernel capture: the presentation as a scanline recipe
tasks.deliverable: a minimal TIA/6507 timing model sufficient to record, per frame, every TIA write with its cycle position, emitted as a raster recipe (the same recipe across tiers); 76 cycles x 262 lines, 3 colour clocks per CPU cycle, WSYNC recognised as the synchroniser
tasks.acceptance: recording a fixture kernel twice yields byte-identical recipes; a frame overruns its 262 lines and the capture reports the overrun instead of truncating it; the recipe is small enough to state its size in bytes and that number is recorded; a recipe replays to the same scanline register state it was captured from
tasks.why_it_is_lawfully_clean: a recipe describes BEHAVIOUR (what the program did to the beam), not EXPRESSION (the pixels it produced) -- and it is also the thing the tier ladder needs, because a handheld drops resolution while replaying the same writes
tasks.risk: HMOVE timing, RESP reset delays and the WSYNC race are where 'almost right' becomes wrong for a 1979 audience. PAL is not NTSC (50 Hz, 312 lines) and the recipe must declare which machine it models or two players will disagree about speed

tasks.title: Integer sim extraction: 128 bytes of state, identified by evidence
tasks.deliverable: identify RAM variables as position/velocity/score/lives/timer by EVIDENCE (read by render, written by input, compared against a threshold) and emit an integer sim + state hash + input transcript; the full game state fits in one hash
tasks.acceptance: the extracted sim replays the recorded input transcript to the observed state hash on >= 3 scenarios; a variable with no evidence is left UNIDENTIFIED and listed rather than guessed; a deliberately mis-classified variable (position read as score) makes the replay diverge and the divergence is reported with the tick
tasks.risk: 128 bytes is the entire game, so a single mis-identified byte is a wrong game. The UNIDENTIFIED list is the honest output, not a failure to hide

tasks.title: Divergence lab: measure the feel, do not argue about it
tasks.deliverable: reuse the M-27 divergence counter over a 2600 scenario matrix (movement, collision, scoring, timing/frame budget, input latency) and publish a divergence count per family with the first-divergence tick
tasks.acceptance: the same scenario recorded twice gives 0 divergences; a one-frame input offset gives > 0 with the first divergent tick named; a scenario of >= 10,000 native ticks runs inside the bench budget and that number is recorded; each scenario family has its own line in the report (a single global 'fidelity: good' is refused)
tasks.risk: zero divergence on one scenario is not fidelity. The matrix exists because the only shard you can fully test is the one you already understand

tasks.title: Bleeding-edge presentation: 3 tiers over one 60 Hz sim, plus CRT as parameters
tasks.deliverable: the M-30 ladder applied to a 2600 revival shard: tier 0 = the original hardware class (160x192, 2-bit-ish palette), tier 1 = corrected aspect + palette, tier 2 = CRT model (scanline gate, phosphor decay, NTSC artefacting as PARAMETERS, no image assets), tier 3 = optional 120/240 Hz presentation of the same recipe; plus verifiable score runs from a transcript + state hash
tasks.acceptance: --verify proves ONE state hash across >= 3 tiers while presentation counters differ; the shard's total payload is stated in bytes and stays inside the M-02 budget; a tier that alters the sim is refused by the existing V7 gate; a score run's transcript re-verifies on a second host
tasks.risk: the temptation is to make tier 3 look like a modern game, which destroys the reason to resurrect it. Tier 0 is the reference and every tier must be able to justify itself as 'the same 1979 picture, seen better'

tasks.title: Audio recipe: extract the patch table, never sample the output
tasks.depends_on_note: independent of M-36; can run in parallel with it
tasks.deliverable: capture the AUDC/AUDF/AUDV write pattern as a patch table (2-bit waveform machine, per-channel frequency divider and volume) and replay it through a small synth; declare the assumed sample rate and the machine (NTSC/PAL)
tasks.acceptance: the same note sequence captured twice gives the same patch table; a capture that cannot resolve a divider is reported as unresolved rather than approximated; the audio is generated from parameters with no audio file in the shard
tasks.risk: sampling the output would be an exact copy of the game's own audio, which is the one thing this whole design exists to avoid. The patch table is lawful because it is the machine's parameters, not the sound

tasks.title: Swordline: the fixed-step orchestrator, with rate and acceleration invariance proved
tasks.deliverable: Project_FLAME/tools/flame_engine.py (DELIVERED 2026-11-01; the game engine belongs to Project FLAME, not FLAMING SWORD): exact rational clock over NTSC 60000/1001 Hz, a Session frame pump that never loses a remainder, a tick-exact comparison path, a Machine seam four methods wide (`reset`/`step`/`state_hash`/`snapshot`) that the 2600 sim plugs into at M-34, and `--verify` running the invariance matrix
tasks.acceptance: DONE 2026-11-01 -- slicing invariance holds (60/120/144/240 fps deliver identical tick counts and identical state hashes at 1x, 2x and 8x); acceleration equivalence holds (the same tick count reached at 1x and 8x gives the same state, in 600 vs 75 frames); no tick served twice and none skipped; the negative control (a clock that assumes every display is 60 Hz, right at 60 fps and 4x too fast at 240 fps) is CAUGHT

evidence.selftest: SELFTEST OK (9 clock controls, 3 machine controls, 4 schedule controls)
evidence.verified_matrix: 599 ticks / identical hash across 60, 120, 144 and 240 fps at 1x; 1198 at 2x; 4795 at 8x; 10 simulated seconds each
evidence.control: 60 Hz-assuming clock: 599 ticks at 60 fps, 2397 at 240 fps -> 2 distinct hashes -> CAUGHT

limits: the machine it drives is a STAND-IN with the 2600's constraints (integer only, bounded state); what is proved is scheduling invariance, not game fidelity -- the output says so in its own `scope` field
there is no renderer: presentation is a state projection until M-36 defines tiers
input is a transcript deterministic in the TICK, which is required for the invariance claim and is also what rollback and replay need
tasks.found_by_its_own_control: the first version of `run_to_ticks` stopped on FRAME boundaries, so at 8x it overshot 299 ticks to 303 and reported a different state -- found by the acceleration test, fixed by adding a tick-exact path
tasks.risk: an orchestrator that cannot be shown to fail is decoration; the 60 Hz-assuming control is the only reason the VERIFIED line means anything

tasks.title: End-to-end cartridge source: no third-party ROM enters this tree
tasks.question: the pipeline needs a real cartridge to exercise end to end; where may it come from?
tasks.decision_2026_11_01: three lawful sources, and a downloaded commercial ROM is not one of them: (1) the owner's own cartridge, which `--inspect` already accepts and which is the entire premise of the track; (2) the synthetic banked fixtures in tests/test_sword_2600.py, which exercise F8/FE/3F geometry and the wrong-hot-spot control; (3) a homebrew cart whose licence the user can show. Searched for a CC0/public-domain 2600 ROM and found none with an explicit licence statement -- Stella's test tree ships only profile and bezel data (git tree queried 2026-11-01) and 8bitworkshop declares no repo-level licence through the API -- so none was downloaded, and the e2e path stays cartridge-in, bytes-never-out
tasks.acceptance: an e2e run is demonstrated on a real image the owner supplies (`sword_2600.py --inspect`), and the fixtures cover the geometry; no binary from a third party is committed; a missing fixture causes the tests to construct their own rather than fetch

tasks.title: The task file has a gate (tools/task_shape_check.py, T1..T5)
tasks.deliverable: tools/task_shape_check.py: T1 shape-complete, T2 predicate-runnable, T3 control-present, T4 evidence-lands, T5 no-acceptance-language; planted in tools/preflight_all.py as the `task-shape` gate so the hook runs it
tasks.acceptance: `python tools/task_shape_check.py --check` exits 0 and prints the shaped count; `--selftest` refuses 7 named mutations and accepts a correctly shaped task it adds itself
tasks.control: set a shaped task's acceptance to the adjective 'good enough' and require T5 to REFUSE it, then blank the command and require T2 to REFUSE that too
tasks.refusal: BLOCK when a shaped task's acceptance names no command or no observable outcome, when its control describes nothing refused, or when its evidence is a promise like TBD
tasks.evidence: stdout of tools/task_shape_check.py --selftest; tests/test_task_shape_check.py drives both directions
tasks.risk: a shape gate that fails legacy tasks retroactively teaches the executor to route around it; legacy tasks are therefore counted and printed, never failed

tasks.title: FLAMING SWORD has a defender prompter (frame before the change, DRAFT when it is still empty)
tasks.deliverable: Project_FLAMING_SWORD/tools/defender.py (D1..D9, render, draft) + `sword.py --defend` + the `protocol.defender` block in aio/flaming_sword.aio.json
tasks.acceptance: `python Project_FLAMING_SWORD/tools/defender.py --selftest` exits 0 with 12 controls; `sword.py --defend '<intent>'` with no evidence prints a DRAFT and exits 0, and the same frame with a named defence but no acceptance command exits 1
tasks.control: set bytes_of_original to 1024 in an otherwise valid posture and require D9 to REFUSE the frame, then cite authority 'vibes' and require the same refusal
tasks.refusal: BLOCK a frame that names no defence, no refused mutation, or no posture on preservation work; a refused frame renders no prompt at all
tasks.risk: a prompter is not a guarantee: it cannot make the work lawful, only make it state whose copy it is; the frame's own rule 3 (quote the command) is what stops a summary from closing a task

tasks.title: The sweep refuses a batch whose items carry no frame
tasks.deliverable: sword.py --run reads .flaming_sword/frames.jsonl (one frame per queue id, written by --defend) and refuses a batch where any id has none; the frame is printed in the before-land decision block
tasks.acceptance: `python Project_FLAMING_SWORD/tools/sword.py --run --batch 1 --test "python -m pytest -q" --dry-run` on a queued id with no frame prints REFUSED and exits 1, and re-running after `--defend` writes that frame makes it proceed (2 runs, 2 verdicts)
tasks.control: delete the frame line for one id in a copy of frames.jsonl and require the runner to REFUSE that batch rather than fill the gap in
tasks.refusal: BLOCK the batch when any id lacks a frame, or when its frame is still a DRAFT with sentinels left in it
tasks.evidence: .flaming_sword/frames.jsonl plus the two dry-run outputs quoted in the commit's Verified: line
tasks.risk: an extra file to keep in step with the queue; the frame is keyed by queue id and a missing key is refused, so drift shows up as a refusal rather than a silent default

tasks.title: The lane board carries the same four fields
tasks.deliverable: a `--board` mode in tools/task_shape_check.py that reads C:/Users/clint/.azazael/telemetry_store.db and reports rows lacking acceptance/control/refusal/evidence, plus a post helper that writes all four
tasks.acceptance: `python tools/task_shape_check.py --board --json` exits 0 and prints the count of rows lacking the four fields; after the backfill it prints 0 of N, and a probe row posted without them is REFUSED locally (1 probe, 1 refusal)
tasks.control: post a probe row carrying only a title and require the checker to count it as unshaped, then require the post helper to REFUSE the same row
tasks.refusal: BLOCK a post that carries no acceptance command, so the first turn cannot claim work the row never defined
tasks.evidence: stdout of tools/task_shape_check.py --board --json before and after the backfill, quoted in lane.freebuff.status
tasks.risk: the board is shared with other lanes and writes go through _board.py; this task must not fork the store or set AZAZAEL_MEMORY_DIR, and it reads first

tasks.title: A retraction is recorded when it happens, not reconstructed at the end
tasks.deliverable: tools/retraction_ledger.py: append-only JSONL (claim, why it was wrong, what replaced it, command that showed it), with `--check` refusing an open retraction older than one turn
tasks.acceptance: `python tools/retraction_ledger.py --check` exits 0 on an empty ledger and glaringly reports 1 open retraction after a planted one; the planted record is REFUSED when its command field is empty (2 verdicts, 2 exits)
tasks.control: append a retraction with no command and require --check to REFUSE it, then add the command and require it to be accepted
tasks.refusal: BLOCK a retracted claim that names no replacement, because a retraction with no successor leaves the wrong claim standing
tasks.evidence: tools/retraction_ledger.py --selftest output plus the ledger file it writes in a temp directory
tasks.risk: easy to turn into a diary; the gate only counts, and a retraction with no materialised trigger is refused the same way a lesson without a decision class is

contract_changes_decided.status: all five accepted before M-01 freeze

items.change: Wasm 3.0 host on the deterministic execution profile, threads and SIMD disabled
items.because: R2 - a shard is currently arbitrary code from a friend's USB; measured: src/INTERPRETERS/* run raw subprocesses with only cwd+timeout; also makes determinism a host property

items.change: one-download player (browser/WASM target) as the distribution unit
items.because: R1 - install-python-first is where a non-author player stops; browser target also gives sandbox for free

items.change: hubs as versioned shared libraries, declared and counted
items.because: R4 - banning external references forces every shard to duplicate its engine inside 24 files; census already models hubs as 'mycelium'

items.change: competitive flag: determinism declared per shard, not required of all
items.because: R3 - the hash chain is a tax against ranked strangers, and a circle has none; solo/puzzle/doc-only shards opt out

items.change: content-addressed shard ids (id@hash) with host-version fallback
items.because: R6 - version skew currently reads to players as a broken game; arena@sha256:... allows coexistence

deferred: visual identity or raised payload budget (R10, M-02)

bleeding_edge_adaptations.status: research recorded 2026-10-31; one contract refinement and one candidate task, neither accepted
bleeding_edge_adaptations.contract_refinement: pending change #1 upgrades from 'sandboxed loader (WASM or restricted VM)' to 'Wasm 3.0 host, deterministic execution profile, threads and SIMD disabled' (Wasm 3.0 completed 2025-09-17; spec 3.0 numerics dated 2026-10-27)
adopted_strands: S3 WASM-4 cartridge as artifact form
avoid: S14 web3 framing: 93% of blockchain games dead by 2024, Abstract chain shutting 2026-12-15, IMX ~-99% from ATH

candidate_tasks.title: Recovery track: a shard wrapping a clean-room recompiled game
candidate_tasks.deliverable: provenance record (raw + sha + url + tier) per artifact; an explicit statement that no original assets ship; one worked example or a recorded decision not to do this
candidate_tasks.acceptance: a written legal position exists before any code; the provenance record validates; the shard runs from the user's own legal copy and ships no original assets
candidate_tasks.risk: legal exposure by jurisdiction; precedents are the N64 recompilation/decompilation scene, which exists in a grey zone

non_goals: any decryption, patching, unlocking or dumping path in the sword -- the M-29 risk note names this as the single change that would turn this project into the thing the 2024 rulemaking refused to protect
shipping an original ROM, cartridge image or game asset inside a shard
a bulk converter that claims to convert a library: per-game work is the honest product
known_limits: discovery is social: a circle works for five friends and fails for five thousand strangers
determinism across hosts needs a numeric policy or the replay verifier will disagree in ways that look like cheating
a cheat inside a shard's own golden run is invisible to the validator; only a peer re-run or an antibody shard catches it
budgets in the plan are commitments to measure, not results
